Mortgageable: ELECTRIC_COMPANY, READING_RAILROAD.

Alternatively, could build a hotel on one property after 4 houses, but need 4 houses on each before hotel? But you need to have 4 houses on each before converting one to hotel? In Monopoly, you must have 4 houses on each property in a color group before you can build a hotel on any of them, and you must build evenly. So to get a hotel, need to have 4 houses on each of the three properties (12 houses total) then replace 4 houses on one property with a hotel (cost same as house? Thus best is to build one house on each orange property. That uses $300, leaves $10 cash. That improves rent significantly. Also could consider mortgaging a property to have more cash for building? Not needed.

Alternatively, could mortgage a property to have cash for building more houses? But we already have enough cash for one house each. Could we also build a fourth house on one property? Wait we need to decide order: we could mortgage reading railroad first, get $100, cash becomes $410, then build houses costing $300, leaving $110 cash. Could we then build a fourth house on one property? That would cost $100, leaving $10. But building must be even across properties: you must build houses evenly. So after having 3 houses each, you could add a fourth house to one property only if the others also have 3? Actually the rule: you must build houses evenly across the color group; you cannot have a difference of more than one house between properties. So after 3 houses each, you could add a fourth house to one property only if you also add a fourth to the others before adding a hotel. So you cannot have 4 houses on one and 3 on others. So you need to add a fourth house to all three to be even, costing $300 more. Not possible.

Thus best is to build one house each, maybe also mortgage a property to keep some cash buffer for rent payments. But after building, cash $10, which is low; if they land on opponent's property with rent >10, they'd need to mortgage or sell houses. Opponents have some properties: Beta has orange? Actually Beta has Kentucky, Indiana, Illinois (red group). Those have high rent. If Alpha lands on those, they'd owe rent. With only $10 cash, they'd be forced to mortgage or sell houses. So maybe better to keep some cash buffer. Could mortgage reading railroad to get $100, then build houses costing $300, leaving cash $110. That seems safer. But we need to consider that mortgaging reduces rent from that property (reading railroad). However, reading railroad rent is low unless they have other railroads. They only have reading railroad, no other railroads. So mortgage reduces potential income but not huge.

Thus optimal: mortgage READING_RAILROAD (or ELECTRIC_COMPANY) to get cash, then build houses. Since we can only take one post-turn action at a time, we must choose one action now. But we have only one action per decision. The scenario says "Choose exactly one post-turn action now. So we could first mortgage reading railroad, then next call build houses, then maybe end turn.

Thus first action: mortgage READING_RAILROAD. Public message: maybe say "Mortgage reading railroad to raise cash for building houses." Could be strategic to inform others? Might be okay.
